featured_reviews.name: Himanshu Dubey
featured_reviews.review_text: I consulted Dr. Vijal in the last week of May after struggling with anxiety and depression for a long time. After the first session of just collecting information about me, she began the intervention and to my absolute surprise she found out some very deep rooted issues that I was neither thinking about nor thought them to be related to the problems I was facing. My initial reaction was denial but I pushed myself to honestly accept them and work on resolving them. She then guided me through,  step by step, one issue at a time and helped me reach a point where I could objectively look at myself, identify the causes of my problems that basically were just thoughts that had buried their roots into my personality causing a multitude of triggers resulting in stress and anxiety. As soon as I worked on those couple of points, I regained control over my thought process and in a matter of four weeks, I started to feel optimistic, relaxed and confident. She helped me regain trust in myself and greatly helped me understand my parents while at the same time gave me the will and confidence to stand up for myself where necessary without guilt or emotional pressure which in a way saved my relationship with them. I am very glad I reached out to her. She is very pleasant with a very transparent and effective approach that is a perfect mix of friendly to make you feel comfortable to open up yet firm to make you work on yourself without any lag.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text: Thank you for your kind words, Himanshu.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I want to share my experience with Dr. Amitabh Ghosh, a psychotherapist who works deeply with trauma, especially childhood trauma, using modalities like psychodrama and EMDR.

When I first started therapy with him, I was in an extremely fragile mental state. I was experiencing schizophrenic-like attacks and hallucinations. My anxiety was so severe that I was scared to step out of my house, scared to take a lift, scared to sit in a car, metro, or any moving vehicle. I was terrified of water bodies, small spaces, and even fears that are hard to explain or imagine. My life felt completely restricted by fear.

We started therapy from that point. It took me some time to understand his working style, but what stood out the most is that he never forces therapy on you. He truly believes that healing happens when you choose it. He creates a space where you arrive at therapy by yourself, in your own readiness, and that philosophy changed everything for me.

Initially, psychodrama was difficult for me because I was very much in my mind, trying to control and intellectualize everything. But as we continued, I slowly built trust, learned to let go, and switched off my analytical mind. That’s when the real transformation began.

What makes Dr. Ghosh different is his deep love and respect for his discipline. I’ve seen him constantly reading, learning, and researching—even between sessions. His commitment to understanding the human mind and trauma at the root level is rare. He doesn’t work on surface symptoms; he always goes to the root cause, and that’s where real healing happens.

My healing journey with him has been incredibly smooth and profound. Today, I can honestly say I’ve reached around 80% of my healing journey, and my entire life has changed. I have worked with multiple therapists before, but he was the last therapist I gave myself a chance with—and it worked in the most magical, almost miraculous way.

If you are looking for help for yourself or a loved one, I highly recommend Dr. Amitabh Ghosh. This is the kind of therapist you should give a genuine try. For me, he has been the best therapeutic guide I’ve ever met.

And if you ever come across this review, I truly believe it’s not a coincidence. Maybe God led you here. Please don’t ignore it—give this a chance.

10/10 recommended.
Love and peace.

owner_posts.post_text: In a world that’s always ‘on,’ the real strength today is knowing when to pause. Feeling mentally drained doesn’t mean you’re failing — it means you’ve been carrying too much for too long. Give yourself permission to rest, unplug, and breathe. Protecting your peace is productivity too.

Summer can affect mental health in different ways. For some people, sunshine and longer days may improve mood. For others, rising temperatures can worsen anxiety, low mood, irritability, fatigue, and poor sleep.

Heat places extra stress on the body, can disturb sleep, and may intensify physical sensations like a racing heart or restlessness, which can feel similar to anxiety. Poor sleep during warmer nights can also affect concentration, emotional balance, and energy levels.

At the same time, simple protective habits can make a real difference: staying hydrated, keeping a regular routine, gentle movement, rest, and spending time in calming natural spaces.

In simple terms: summer can boost mood when the body is well-regulated. Prioritising sleep, hydration, and rest is not just self-care~it is mental health care.

We at Mindsight encourage you to stay hydrated, slow down when needed, and take gentle care of your mind and body this summer. ☀️

Sitting with your feelings means noticing them, allowing them, and understanding they will pass.

Name the emotion, feel it without judgment, and meet yourself with kindness. 💙

In this community, every feeling is valid and welcome.

Resilience check-in 🌱

We often think resilient people have it all together… but the truth is, they feel overwhelmed too.

Resilience isn’t about avoiding hard moments – it’s about how we move through them, in our own time and in our own way.

Feel free to share, reflect, or just pause here for a moment. You don’t have to have it all figured out. 🌱

In a world that’s always ‘on,’ the real strength today is knowing when to pause. Feeling mentally drained doesn’t mean you’re failing — it means you’ve been carrying too much for too long. Give yourself permission to rest, unplug, and breathe. Protecting your peace is productivity too.

Setting boundaries isn’t selfish — it’s essential. When you protect your time, energy, and emotional space, you protect your mental health. Saying no, stepping back, or choosing yourself is not wrong; it’s healthy. Boundaries help you breathe, heal, and grow.

Therapists want you to know this:

•Choosing therapy isn’t weakness — it’s quiet courage.
•It’s the strength of saying, I deserve to feel lighter.
•Healing begins the moment you decide you don’t have to carry it alone.

Self-Discipline vs Self-Compassion: 

Which one actually helps you stay consistent?

We’re often taught that strict self-discipline and self-criticism are the keys to success. 

But research and clinical experience show that self-compassion—being kind, understanding, and realistic with yourself—actually leads to better consistency over time. 

When you respond to mistakes with curiosity instead of harsh judgment, you reduce shame, build emotional safety, and make it easier to try again.

Self-discipline rooted in self-compassion isn’t about “letting yourself off the hook”; it’s about supporting yourself in a way that makes growth sustainable, not exhausting. 🌱

As we step into April, let’s take a gentle pause to check in with ourselves. Mental health is just as important as physical health—small steps like rest, talking to someone, or taking mindful breaks can make a big difference. 💚

Let’s support each other in creating a safe, understanding space where everyone feels heard and valued.

You may struggle with self-doubt, shame, insecurity, harsh self-criticism, body image concerns, or a deeper confusion about who you are and what you really want. In therapy, I do not offer surface-level confidence advice. I help you understand how these patterns developed, why they keep repeating, and what may be needed for real change. My style is reflective, depth-oriented, and emotionally engaged. Therapy can help you build a more stable sense of self, reduce self-attack, trust your own mind more, make clearer decisions, and begin living with greater confidence, authenticity, and self-respect.

Trauma Therapy

Trauma can continue affecting you long after the painful event is over. It may show up as fear, emotional overwhelm, numbness, mistrust, shame, panic, relationship difficulties, or feeling that the past is still shaping how you respond in the present. Sometimes people do not even think of their experience as trauma, but they know something in them still feels unsettled, guarded, or deeply hurt. In therapy, I work in a paced, respectful, and emotionally containing way. My approach is depth-oriented and sensitive to both emotional safety and the deeper impact of painful experiences. The aim is not to force you to relive what happened, but to help you process it, understand its effects, reduce its hold on your life, and gradually build a stronger sense of safety, stability, and emotional freedom.

Overthinking and OCD Therapy

Overthinking and OCD can leave you feeling trapped inside your own mind. You may keep replaying things, doubting yourself, checking, analysing, seeking reassurance, or struggling with intrusive thoughts that feel upsetting, confusing, or hard to control. These patterns can take away peace of mind, drain energy, and make even simple decisions feel exhausting. In therapy, I work with both the distress you are facing and the deeper emotional patterns that may be keeping these cycles active. My style is careful, non-judgmental, and psychologically in-depth, while still practical enough to help you respond differently in daily life. Therapy can help you reduce the grip of obsessive thinking, feel less controlled by fear and doubt, and regain a greater sense of freedom, clarity, and trust in yourself.

Depression Therapy

Depression is not always obvious from the outside. Sometimes it looks like low mood, tiredness, emptiness, irritability, loss of interest, emotional numbness, crying spells, or simply feeling stuck in survival mode. It can affect motivation, sleep, work, relationships, and your sense of meaning in life. In therapy, I offer a space where your suffering is taken seriously and explored with care. My approach is thoughtful, emotionally attentive, and depth-oriented, with focus on both what is happening now and what may be shaping it underneath. Therapy can help you understand what is weighing you down, reduce self-criticism, reconnect with yourself, and slowly begin to feel more alive, more hopeful, and more able to engage with life again in a meaningful way.

Anxiety Therapy

Anxiety can make daily life feel heavy, tense, and difficult to switch off from. You may find yourself constantly worrying, overthinking, feeling restless, panicky, physically on edge, or expecting something to go wrong even when things seem fine on the surface. Over time, anxiety can affect sleep, work, relationships, confidence, and your ability to feel settled in yourself. In therapy, I help you understand not only the symptoms, but also the emotional patterns and pressures that may be driving them. My style is calm, thoughtful, and depth-oriented, while still practical and grounded. The aim is not just temporary relief, but a deeper sense of steadiness, better emotional regulation, clearer thinking, and the ability to face life with more confidence and less fear.

Anger and Emotional Regulation Therapy

Anger often carries more beneath it than people realise. It may involve frustration, hurt, resentment, helplessness, shame, or feeling repeatedly misunderstood and overwhelmed. When anger shows up as irritability, harsh tone, emotional outbursts, jealousy, impulsive reactions, or difficulty calming down, it can damage relationships, create tension at work or home, and leave you feeling guilty afterward. In therapy, I help you understand not just the anger itself, but what happens inside you before it escalates. My style is direct, thoughtful, and emotionally focused, without being shaming or moralistic. Therapy can help you become less reactive, regulate emotions better, communicate more clearly, and respond with more control, maturity, and steadiness in difficult situations.

Some messages stay with you. 🌿

A young student I supported during her board exam phase recently wrote to share that she scored 98 and felt that our work together helped her stay calmer, steadier, and able to function well under pressure.

Moments like these are deeply meaningful. Academic performance is never only about intelligence or effort; emotional containment, clarity, and psychological support can make a real difference when it matters most.

Grateful to be trusted in such important phases of people’s lives.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I started therapy with Dr. Tejas Shah during the COVID period in 2020, when I was in a very difficult mental state. Living near Worli sea face, constantly hearing ambulance sirens, reading about COVID, and knowing that older people and those with heart problems were more vulnerable made me extremely anxious. I stopped going out, lost 12 kg, stopped working, and gradually slipped into mild depression. Even basic daily routines became difficult.

Although I was advised to take antidepressants, I was not in favor of psychotropic medication. On the recommendation of my psychologist, I began talk therapy with Dr. Tejas Shah—initially twice a week, and later up to five times a week.

Over time, therapy helped me not only with the fear and distress of that period, but also with long-standing issues of self-doubt, self-criticism, lack of confidence, and feeling “not good enough.” Since 2024, I have gradually reduced therapy to twice a week, which I continue till now (April 2026).

Today, I feel much more relaxed, less self-critical, and more socially at ease. I enjoy conversations, feel more spontaneous, and am much less shy than before. I also see the difference in my professional work. I am calmer with patients, more attentive, and more confident in explaining medical as well as psychological aspects of their condition. I feel I am maturing into a better Psycho-Dermatologist.

At the age of 80, I continue to work, pursue my PhD, journal daily, and stay mentally active. I still have some challenges, such as anxiety before presentations, but I can clearly see how much progress I have made.

I find Dr. Tejas Shah to be a very good analyst—patient, attentive, and a deeply thoughtful listener. His integrative therapy approach has helped bring about meaningful change in my life. I intend to continue therapy with him, now twice a week, for as long as my mind permits.
